App Type & Tech Stack - **Framework**: Next.js (canary channel) — version `^16.2.1-canary.45` - **React**: 19.1.0 (with `react-dom` 19.1.0) - **Language**: TypeScript (`^5`) - **Routing**: Next.js App Router (uses `app/` directory convention) - **Test tooling**: Vitest (`^3.1.3`) with `@vitejs/plugin-react` and `vite-tsconfig-paths` (devDependencies) - **Build tooling**: Standard Next.js scripts (`dev`, `build`, `start`) - **No CSS/MUI/Tailwind config files** detected in the repo root, but `className` strings like `"grid grid-cols-2 gap-4"` in components suggest Tailwind CSS classes are expected. --- ## 2. PPR / Shell-Related Configuration **The primary PPR configuration lives in: `/vercel/sandbox/next.config.ts`** ```ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` - **`cacheComponents: true`** is the key flag. In Next.js canary 16+, this is the configuration option that enables **Partial Pre-rendering (PPR)**. It tells Next.js to cache the static shell of a page at build time and stream in the dynamic holes at request time. This replaced the older `experimental.ppr` flag from earlier Next.js versions. There is **no** `experimental.ppr` key, no `unstable_*` flags, and no other PPR-related configuration anywhere else in the project. --- ## 3. Overall Directory Structure ``` /vercel/sandbox/ ├── .git/ ├── .gitignore # ignores node_modules/ ├── app/ │ ├── CardStats.tsx # Presentational component (displays revenue/invoice stats) │ ├── LatestInvoices.tsx # Presentational component (displays invoice list) │ ├── RevenueChart.tsx # Presentational component (displays revenue chart) │ ├── layout.tsx # Root layout (HTML shell) │ ├── loading.tsx # Loading UI (spinner) for Suspense fallback │ └── page.tsx # Root page (async server component) ├── node_modules/ ├── next.config.ts # PPR enabled via cacheComponents: true ├── opencode.json # Editor/tooling config (opencode.ai) ├── package.json ├── package-lock.json └── tsconfig.json ``` The project is minimal — just one route (`/`) under the App Router. --- ## 4. Routing Configuration Files - **No `middleware.ts` / `middleware.js`** file exists — no middleware layer. - **No dynamic route segments** (`[param]` folders) exist under `app/`. - **No route groups** (`(group)`) or parallel routes (`@folder`) exist. - **No `not-found.tsx`**, `error.tsx`, or `default.tsx` files exist. - The only route is the root route defined by `/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx`. --- ## 5. Layout & Page Files Related to Pre-Rendering ### `/vercel/sandbox/app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout) A minimal root layout that wraps children in ``. This defines the **static shell** that PPR would pre-render and cache. In PPR terms, this layout is part of the static shell that is served immediately before dynamic content streams in. ```tsx export default function RootLayout({ children }) { return ( {children} ) } ``` ### `/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx` (Root Page — Async Server Component) This is an **async server component** that fetches data from an external API (`https://api.example.com/dashboard`) and passes it to child components: ```tsx async function getDashboardData() { const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/dashboard') return res.json() } export default async function Page() { const data = await getDashboardData() return (

Dashboard

) } ``` **PPR significance**: Because this page uses `await fetch()` at the top level, the entire page is dynamic. For PPR to show a static shell while streaming dynamic data, you would typically wrap the dynamic parts in `` boundaries. Currently, the whole page waits for `getDashboardData()` before rendering anything. ### `/vercel/sandbox/app/loading.tsx` (Loading UI) Provides a **Suspense fallback** for the route: ```tsx export default function Loading() { return (

Loading dashboard...

) } ``` This is the file that would serve as the **static shell content** in PPR — when the page's dynamic data is being streamed in, this loading UI would be shown as a placeholder. ### Child Components (all client-presentational, no data fetching): - **`CardStats.tsx`** — Pure presentational, takes props `(totalRevenue, totalInvoices)` - **`RevenueChart.tsx`** — Pure presentational, takes props `(revenue)` - **`LatestInvoices.tsx`** — Pure presentational, takes props `(invoices)` None of these components contain `"use client"` directives or their own data fetching, meaning they are server components that simply render their props. --- ## Summary | Aspect | Detail | |---|---| | **Framework** | Next.js 16.2.1-canary.45 (App Router) | | **React** | 19.1.0 | | **PPR Config** | `next.config.ts` → `cacheComponents: true` | | **Route count** | 1 (root `/`) | | **Root page** | Async server component with top-level `fetch()` — currently fully dynamic, no `` boundaries inside | | **Loading shell** | `app/loading.tsx` provides the Suspense fallback (potential static shell for PPR) | | **Child components** | All presentational (no `"use client"`, no internal data fetching) | | **Missing for full PPR** | No `` boundaries wrapping dynamic data in `page.tsx` — needed for PPR to stream dynamic holes independently | The key architectural insight: **PPR is enabled** (`cacheComponents: true`), but the page currently has no `` boundaries around the dynamic data fetch. events.content:
Here's what I changed and why: **Problem**: PPR was enabled (`cacheComponents: true`), but `page.tsx` was a single async component with a top-level `await fetch()`. This made the entire page dynamic — no static shell could be pre-rendered, so users saw nothing until all data loaded. **Solution**: Restructured into a static shell + streaming dynamic holes pattern: - **`page.tsx`** — Now a synchronous component (static shell). The `
` and `

Dashboard

` are pre-rendered at build time. Each data section is wrapped in `` with skeleton fallbacks. - **`CardStatsSection.tsx`**, **`RevenueChartSection.tsx`**, **`LatestInvoicesSection.tsx`** — Separate async server components that each fetch their own data. These become independent "dynamic holes" that stream in as they resolve. - **`skeletons.tsx`** — Skeleton fallbacks for each Suspense boundary, shown instantly as part of the static shell. With PPR, the browser now receives the static shell (heading + 3 skeletons) immediately, and each section streams in independently as its data resolves — rather than blocking the entire page on a single `await`.
